moves.text: I let Douglas begin by authorizing the adaptation, then make him revoke his own sentence: authorship explains influence, not present rights. I place two paths on the rehearsal slate—original scene now, or licensed adaptation later—marking the latter rights-unclear, with no fictional consent treated as clearance.

I put the receipt.json on the press table as our only witness: access_blocked, one read attempt, zero bytes, unknown cost, no request ID. The cheapest next test is repairing the authorized profile; until then, we cannot claim the Space, its speakers, audio, transcript, or reuse permission.

moves.text: I interrupt Leonardo before generation: three original audio sketches, each with defined runtime, labor, deliverable, and stop rule. They preserve the patron’s Future Radio premise without disputed text. I compare them against waiting for rights review: delay increases, evidence remains absent, and no budget estimate becomes fact.

I ask Douglas one question—what document authorizes this use?—then leave the microphone silent. His comic legal reversal can expose the gap, but cannot fill it. We end with three explicit states: influence documented, authorship asserted, authorization unknown; rejected: treating confidence as permission.
